disease_label_per_paper: Bartonella henselae culture-negative infective endocarditis of a Melody valve
presentation_summary: 32-year-old man with repaired tetralogy of Fallot, RV-to-pulmonary artery conduit, and Melody valve presented with one month of intermittent fever to 103 F, chills, dyspnea on exertion, and intermittent non-pruritic upper-extremity macular rash.
Initial vitals included blood pressure 101/71 mmHg, heart rate 99/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air; exam showed a grade III/VI systolic ejection murmur and Janeway lesions on the right toe.
Labs showed pancytopenia, creatinine 2.17 mg/dL, large blood and protein on urinalysis, proBNP 13275 pg/mL, CRP 3.1 mg/dL, and ESR 71 mm/hr.
TTE showed a small mobile mass in the proximal RVOT and moderate to severe RVOT obstruction with peak and mean gradients of 80 and 46 mmHg.
Routine blood cultures remained negative; Bartonella serology was positive with high IgG titers, and AKI was attributed to immune-complex glomerulonephritis secondary to endocarditis.

quality_warnings: Bartonella serology is confirmatory and is not included as an ordinary observation.
